port.name: Lazydocker
port.description: Living Code for Lazydocker: native YAML overrides for active/inactive borders, selected rows and option text in four flavors.

guide.installation:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/living-code-theme/lazydocker.git
cd lazydocker
```

Open your Lazydocker config using the project panel’s **o** action. Merge `gui.theme` from the selected file in `themes/`, replacing existing theme keys while preserving all Docker commands and other settings.

Default locations: Linux `~/.config/lazydocker/config.yml`; macOS `~/Library/Application Support/jesseduffield/lazydocker/config.yml`; Windows `%APPDATA%\lazydocker\config.yml`. Restart Lazydocker after saving.
guide.configuration: Only the four exposed theme attributes are changed: `activeBorderColor`, `inactiveBorderColor`, `selectedLineBgColor`, and `optionsTextColor`. Each is the native array of color/style attributes. Active borders are bold. Do not replace your full config with the fragment unless you intentionally want all other settings to return to defaults.
guide.compatibility: For Lazydocker’s `gui.theme` attribute API with hex-color support. This is intentionally a partial UI theme: terminal foreground/background, container health labels and other hard-coded colors are not individually configurable by this API. Use a matching Living Code terminal palette. Tests validate native YAML and the exact field contract; no Docker daemon is needed for maintenance.
